checked.claim: run_frontend() rewrites the surface (2人->二人, ASCII->full-width), so spans must be re-anchored with a custom NFKC+find routine (ja_nodes)
checked.evidence: run_frontend('2人')[0]['string'] == '二人' is confirmed. However, pyopenjtalk-plus 0.4.1.post9 also ships pyopenjtalk.g2p_mapping(text), which returns 'char_span' into the ORIGINAL input plus read/pron/phonemes per surface. Verified: 'ｶﾞｯｺｳ'->(0,5), '1000'->surface 千 span (0,4), '14日'->十四日 span (2,5), 'R','&','B' -> separate spans, '100%' -> 百(7,10) + ％(10,11).
checked.correction: Use pyopenjtalk.g2p_mapping() for Japanese spans. The hand-written re-anchoring heuristic is not needed.

checked.claim: `pron` gives ー long vowels, は->ワ and を->オ
checked.evidence: は->ワ (今日は->キョーワ) and へ->エ (未来へ->ミライエ) are confirmed, and long vowels are marked with ー. But pron keeps particle を as ヲ (地球を回せ -> チキューヲマワセ; g2p_mapping also gives read=ヲ, pron=ヲ). The prototype's own kana table maps を/ヲ->'o', so its output is still correct.
checked.correction: pron does not convert を; the romanization table must (and does) map ヲ->o.

The uroman README itself says kanji are romanized as Chinese.

checked.claim: Custom Hepburn mora table is preferable to uroman for Japanese
checked.evidence: For plain kana the table is identical to uroman (shi/chi/tsu/fu/ji/zu, を->o, ん->n). uroman is inconsistent on extended katakana: ふぁ->fua, てぃ->tei but ティ->ti, でゅ->deyu, うぃ->ui, シェ->shie, ヴァ->vua. The report's fa/ti/dyu/wi/she/va is more phonetic and mora-exact. One small gap: ヵ/ヶ map to ''.

checked.claim: g2pk2 keeps block count for pure hangul but is wrong on numbers/English and some rules (꽃잎을->꼰니블, 24시간->이사시간, 2명의->이명의, 10년->심년, baby->베이비, R&B->아&비, whole-line 날려->랄려); ~15 ms/call

checked.claim: Prototype lyricsprep.py works and all span round-trip asserts pass

My extra probes found number bugs. 20살 -> 스물 should be 스무 (native 20 before a counter). 1번째 -> 한 번째 should be 첫 번째. 1번 타자 -> 한 번 should be 일 번 (Sino ordinal), though this one is flagged needs_review. Gikun via markup (本気(マジ), 地球(ほし)) works.

checked.claim: Runtime: ~1.8-6 s cold start (OpenJTalk ~2 s, g2pk2+mecab ~1.5 s, cmudict 0.15 s), ~6.5 ms/line warm
checked.evidence: The machine was at load average 45-60 from parallel agents. Measured: pyopenjtalk import 1.0-2.0 s, g2pk2 init 1.1-5.5 s, cmudict.dict() 0.9-5.3 s, and uroman Uroman() init 5.8-25 s. Full parse of 63 lines took 7.8-8.6 s wall. The report leaves out uroman init, which is the largest single cold-start cost. Warm per-line cost is negligible either way, and this is offline prep, so it does not affect the decision.

checked.claim: For char-level CTC, Korean liaison leaves the character sequence unchanged; only the syllable boundary attribution moves
checked.evidence: Holds by construction, since uroman per-syllable concatenation equals whole-word (ggoc+ip+eul = ggo+ci+peul as a letter string). Corollary the report misses: liaison needs no G2P at all. Align the orthographic letters, then reassign the coda letters to the next syllable when that syllable starts with ㅇ, using a ~20-line jamo rule. Also, MMS was trained on ORTHOGRAPHIC uroman, so the g2pk2 'pron' variant may score worse. The report's per-song CTC-score selection is a reasonable hedge but is still unmeasured.

checked.claim: g2pk3 1.4 (MIT) adds Japanese transliteration and a rule-20 fix
checked.evidence: The PyPI description says '제20조항 오류 문제 해결' and '일본어 발음 전사 추가'. It requires jamo, g2p_en and pyopenjtalk.

recommendation_assessment:
The architecture is sound and the facts it rests on largely check out. The report recommends a deterministic, span-indexed Song->Line->Word->Syllable->AlignUnit tree, with pyopenjtalk-plus for Japanese readings, per-syllable uroman for Korean, CMUdict-count plus pyphen-split for English, and sung-order expansion of repeats and sections. Versions, licenses, wheel availability, torchaudio MMS_FA/forced_align availability in 2.11.0, the uroman behaviour and the g2pk2 bugs and side effects all reproduced, and the prototype runs with all span asserts passing. I would change six things:

(1) Japanese spans. Replace the hand-written ja_nodes() re-anchoring with pyopenjtalk.g2p_mapping(), already in the installed 0.4.1.post9. It returns char_span into the original text, verified on half-width kana, 1000->千 and 14日->十四日.

(2) Japanese reading choice. Use pyopenjtalk.run_mecab_nbest_features() to produce alternatives for heteronyms (今日 キョウ/コンニチ, 何 ナニ/ナン, 明日 アシタ/アス) and pick the one with the higher CTC score on the vocal stem. Install the [onnxruntime] extra (何 model) and consider [tsqyomi]. Keep recurring lyric readings in a pyopenjtalk user dictionary via update_global_jtalk_with_user_dict with is_reading_protected. J-pop gikun (宇宙=そら, 本気=マジ, 地球=ほし) still cannot be inferred. Flag low-confidence words for operator review, and optionally pre-fill furigana suggestions with an LLM or ASR on the separated vocal.

(3) Korean. Make g2pk2 optional, not default. Orthographic uroman matches MMS training, and liaison can be applied after alignment by moving coda letters to the next syllable. Dropping g2pk2 removes the nltk download at import, the pip-install subprocess and the Python ≤3.12 cap. 3.12 is still a fine project default. If a pronunciation variant is wanted, g2pkiwi (kiwipiepy, abi3) avoids python-mecab-ko.

(4) Korean numbers. Fix the native-numeral prenominal forms (스무 살, 첫 번째) and treat 번 as ambiguous. kiwipiepy's SN+NNB tags give a more robust number+counter detector than a suffix list.

(5) Aligner-agnostic output. The alignment track is evaluating Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B, which takes native ja/ko/en text, but its model card lists only 'Speech' audio, so singing is untested. Every unit should therefore expose native-script text plus char spans, not only `roman`.

(6) torchaudio. Note that torchaudio is frozen at 2.11.0 (forward-compatible with torch 2.14 per its release notes). Since 2.9, torchaudio.load/save are implemented on TorchCodec, so load audio with soundfile or librosa.
missed_options: pyopenjtalk.g2p_mapping() (pyopenjtalk-plus >=0.4.1.post9): per-surface char_span into the original input, plus read/pron/phonemes. It removes the custom NFKC+find re-anchoring.
pyopenjtalk.run_mecab_nbest_features(text, max_paths): N-best readings for heteronyms, which can be scored acoustically with the MMS_FA emission to pick the sung reading automatically.

pyopenjtalk-plus extras: [onnxruntime] for the 何 なに/なん classifier and [tsqyomi] for a context-aware heteronym reading model from Hugging Face. Also the user dictionary (update_global_jtalk_with_user_dict with UserDictionaryEntry(is_reading_protected=True)) for recurring lyric gikun.

Dependency-free Korean liaison (연음): align orthographic uroman letters, then move the coda consonant tokens to the next ㅇ-initial syllable using jamo arithmetic. This replaces g2pk2 for the timing-relevant effect.
g2pkiwi 0.1.0 (Apache-2.0, 2022, g2pK fork on kiwipiepy abi3 wheels): avoids python-mecab-ko and the Python ≤3.12 cap if a pronunciation variant is still wanted.
kiwipiepy 0.24.0 morphological tags (SN number + NNB counter) for native vs Sino-Korean numeral choice, instead of a hard-coded counter suffix list.

Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B (qwen-asr 0.0.6, Apache-2.0): native-script ja/ko/en forced alignment. The front-end should also emit native text units and spans for it; its card lists audio type 'Speech' only, so singing needs testing. stable-ts align() and ctc-forced-aligner 1.0.2 (an MMS wrapper with uroman, star token and chunking) are other consumers worth keeping compatible.
ASR on the separated vocal (e.g. Qwen3-ASR, which lists singing/BGM support) or LLM-suggested furigana, to surface gikun and reading mismatches for operator review before alignment.
Raw CMUdict data file (BSD-style) instead of the GPL-3.0 `cmudict` PyPI wrapper if closed-source distribution matters (the report lists this only as an open question).
Load audio with soundfile/librosa rather than torchaudio.load: since torchaudio 2.9, load/save are implemented on TorchCodec, which adds a dependency.
